the Tiberias mishna (38b), whose Festival seifa is quoted at 39b.3
R' Yehuda (bar Ilai), in the 39b.4 and 40b.4 baraitot
Rebbi (R' Yehuda HaNasi): printed (רב) [רבי] at 39b.6; the master of the 40b.8 incident
teaches Rav's ruling in his own version (40a.4); subject of Rav Yosef's question; 'מר' of Abaye's dictum
narrates the Bnei Brak incident (40a.8; Steinsaltz: Rabbi Yehuda); transmits Shmuel at 40b.7 and 40b.10 (printed רבי יהודה at 40b.7)
the Sages of the bathhouse narratives (40a.8-9)
the anonymous first tanna of the 40b.4 baraita (the jug of water)

props.gloss_en: the stam: the 'bathing' forbidden in the Tiberias mishna is washing the face, hands and feet
the mishna's seifa: on a Festival [the water] is like water heated on a Festival -- forbidden for bathing, permitted for drinking
Beit Shammai: a person may not heat water for his feet [on a Festival] unless it is fit for drinking
Beit Hillel permit [heating water for his feet on a Festival]
Rav Ika bar Chananya: [the mishna] deals with rinsing the whole body with [the water]
Rav Ika bar Chananya: and [the mishna] is this tanna's [of the following baraita]
one may not rinse his whole body with hot water (R' Meir; R' Yehuda: בחמין אסור)
R' Meir: one may not rinse his whole body even with cold water
R' Shimon permits [rinsing the whole body] with hot water
rinsing the whole body with cold water is permitted (R' Shimon; R' Yehuda)
the stam: the incident of the people of Tiberias was in [water in] the ground, and the Rabbis forbade them
Rav Chisda, version 1: the dispute is about [water] in a vessel; in the ground all agree it is permitted
Rav Chisda, version 2 (as the stam corrects the report): the dispute is about [water] in the ground; in a vessel all agree it is forbidden
R' Yochanan: the halakha [on rinsing the whole body] follows R' Yehuda
Rabba bar bar Chana heard the ruling explicitly [from R' Yochanan], not by inference
Rebbi: wherever you find two who disagree and one who decides between them, the halakha follows the decider
Rebbi: except the leniencies of strips of cloth -- R' Eliezer is stringent, R' Yehoshua lenient, R' Akiva decides, and the halakha is not as the decider
first, because R' Akiva is a student [of the two disputants]
and moreover, R' Akiva retracted in favour of R' Yehoshua
Rav: water heated on Shabbat eve -- the next day one washes his whole body with it, limb by limb
Shmuel: they permitted washing [with it] only the face, hands and feet
the baraita: water heated on Shabbat eve -- the next day one washes his face, hands and feet with it, but not his whole body
the baraita: they permitted washing with water heated on Shabbat eve only the face, hands and feet
the baraita: [with water heated on Shabbat eve] one washes face, hands and feet, but not his whole body even limb by limb -- and all the more so water heated on a Festival
Rav, as Rabba taught it: one bathes his whole body with it, leaving out one limb
does Rabba act in accordance with Rav's ruling [bathing in pre-heated water on Shabbat]?
Abaye: in all matters the Master acts as Rav [except these three]
Abaye: except these three, where he acts as Shmuel -- one transfers [tzitzit] from garment to garment
Abaye: and one lights from lamp to lamp
Abaye: and the halakha follows R' Shimon on dragging
a bathhouse whose openings were sealed on Shabbat eve -- after Shabbat one bathes in it immediately
sealed on Festival eve -- the next day one enters and sweats, and goes out and rinses in the outer room

Rav Yehuda: in the Bnei Brak bathhouse, sealed on Festival eve, R' Elazar ben Azarya and R' Akiva entered on the Festival, sweated, and rinsed in the outer room -- but its hot water was covered with boards
the Sages: [it is permitted] even if its hot water is not covered with boards
and when transgressors multiplied, they began to forbid [sweating in the bathhouse]
the large bathhouses of cities -- one strolls through them and need not be concerned
bar Kappara: at first people would bathe [on Shabbat] in water heated on Shabbat eve (his answer to מאי עוברי עבירה)
the bath attendants began to heat on Shabbat and say 'it was heated on Shabbat eve'
the Sages forbade [bathing in] hot water [even heated on Shabbat eve]
and permitted sweating (later forbidden)
they still bathed in hot water and said 'we are sweating'
they forbade sweating to them -- and [at the end] the sweating [prohibition] remained in place
they still bathed in fire-heated water and said 'we bathed in the Tiberias springs'
they forbade them the Tiberias springs (later re-permitted)
and permitted them cold water
seeing the matter did not stand for them, they permitted them the Tiberias springs
the reason for re-permitting Tiberias: the decree was not being upheld
Rava: one who violates [a decree of] the Rabbis may be called a transgressor
Rava: specifically [the bathhouses of] cities; but of villages, no
the stam: since they are small, their heat is great
a person may warm himself opposite the fire and go out and rinse in cold water
provided he does not rinse in cold water and then warm himself opposite the fire
because he warms the water that is on him
a person may heat a towel and lay it on his belly on Shabbat
provided he does not bring a kettle of hot water and lay it on his belly on Shabbat
and this is forbidden even on a weekday
because of the danger
a person may bring a jug of water and put it opposite the fire -- not so that it heats, but so that its chill departs
R' Yehuda: a woman may bring a flask of oil and put it opposite the fire -- not so that it cooks, but so that it warms
RSbG: a woman may oil her hand, warm it opposite the fire, and oil her small son, and need not be concerned
the first tanna permits [warming] oil -- even where the hand recoils from it (Rabba and Rav Yosef)
the first tanna forbids [warming] oil -- even where the hand does not recoil from it (Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak)
oil is not subject to [the prohibition of] cooking
oil is subject to [the prohibition of] cooking
warming oil [to lukewarm] is not its cooking
warming oil [to lukewarm] is its cooking
[on Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak's reading] RSbG's position is the same as the first tanna's
the difference between them is [warming oil] in a backhanded manner
Shmuel: oil and water alike -- [heating to where] the hand recoils from it is forbidden
Shmuel: [heating to where] the hand does not recoil from it is permitted
Rachava: [the hand recoils] wherever a baby's belly would be scalded
Rebbi, when R' Yitzchak bar Avdimi sought to put a flask of oil in the bath for him: take [water] in a second vessel and put [the oil in it]
a second vessel does not cook
R' Yochanan: everywhere one may contemplate [Torah] except in the bathhouse and the privy
Abaye: secular matters may be said in the holy tongue [in the bathhouse]
Abaye: holy matters may not be said [there] even in a secular language
the stam: separating [someone] from a prohibition is different
R' Meir to his student in the bathhouse: one does not rinse [the floor]
R' Meir: one does not smear [the floor with oil]
Ravina: one who cooks in the Tiberias hot springs on Shabbat is liable
Rav Chisda: one who cooks in the Tiberias hot springs on Shabbat is exempt
the stam: the 'liable' Ravina said means [liable to] lashes of rebelliousness
R' Zeira: I saw R' Abbahu floating in a bath [on Shabbat]
the stam: it is obvious that he did not lift [his feet]
the baraita: a person may not float in a pool full of water, even one standing in a courtyard
the stam: this [baraita] is a pool without embankments; that [bath] had embankments

questions.gloss_en: Rav Yosef to Abaye: does Rabba act on Rav's ruling? Abaye: I do not know -- and the stam's analysis (40a.5-6) ends without settling it
R' Zeira: I do not know whether R' Abbahu lifted [his feet] or not -- the stam's attempt to settle it is deflected

objections.gloss_en: אימא סיפא: on a Festival... forbidden for bathing -- לימא תנן סתמא כבית שמאי? דתנן: BS forbid heating water for one's feet unless fit to drink, and BH permit; if 'bathing' were face, hands and feet, the anonymous mishna would follow Beit Shammai

והא מעשה דאנשי טבריה בקרקע הוה ואסרי להו רבנן -- the Tiberias water was in the ground and the Rabbis forbade it, so 'in the ground all permit' cannot stand; the stam then re-reports the dictum (אלא אי איתמר הכי איתמר)
מיתיבי: face, hands and feet but not the whole body -- תיובתא דרב (provisional; reversed by the answer)

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר לך רב: 'not the whole body' -- at once, but limb by limb [it is permitted]. [Counter: והא פניו ידיו ורגליו קתני! -- answered: כעין פניו ידיו ורגליו, i.e. limb by limb like those; the counter-round cannot be encoded as an attack on this answer]

objections.gloss_en: תא שמע: they permitted washing with water heated on Shabbat eve only face, hands and feet

answered_by.gloss_en: הכא נמי כעין פניו ידיו ורגליו -- here too, [limb by limb] like face, hands and feet

objections.gloss_en: היכי עביד הכי? והאמר רבה בר בר חנה אמר רבי יוחנן: one may not contemplate [Torah] in the bathhouse. וכי תימא he said it in a secular language -- והאמר אביי: holy matters may not be said there in a secular language [pre-empted deflection; no construct]
